rows.10:d54c: and swung it down at Aizawa.{p}
rows.10:d58c:
"Wh... What are you...!"
How should I describe the sound it made?
Yes, how can I put it...
The sound of something slicing through the air and the sound of something slicing through flesh are surprisingly alike, you know.
That's what I thought, anyway...
Caught off guard, Aizawa struck his head on the floor as he went down, and lost consciousness.
And then Aizawa was... pushed off the roof.
Aizawa wasn't the only one who wanted to push someone off the roof.
And of course, I had been waiting too... waiting all along for Aizawa to fall...{p}
rows.10:d784:
Oh my, what a face you're making.
I'm sorry, I put that in a way that invites misunderstanding.
I wasn't the one who pushed Aizawa off the roof.
The boy I mentioned earlier is just some boy from some other class.
I watched everything that happened between them, from beginning to end.
I like going up to the roof too, you see, so I had been observing their exchanges with great interest.
What became of Aizawa after he was pushed?
I only witnessed things up to the moment he was pushed.
I didn't want to be suspected, so I ran off right away.
Naturally, I never saw his body either.
...Perhaps that boy had been watching for a chance to push Aizawa off all along.
I stayed home from school for several days after that.
What if they knew I had been watching them that day?
Whenever I thought that, I couldn't bring myself to leave the house.{p}
rows.10:daa0:
When I went back to school, all sorts of rumors were going around about the Aizawa incident.
I did my best not to listen to any of them.
I didn't want anything more to do with that incident.
But there is one thing that bothers me.{p}
rows.10:dc3c:
Somehow, it all seems like something from long ago.
Yes, it's a tale of the past.
Of the distant, distant past...
Was what I saw real?
I feel there's only one way to find out.
You go up to the roof and try speaking to Aizawa.{p}
rows.10:ddb4:
He stopped himself.
Then he left Kuwabata where he lay and walked away from the roof.{p}
rows.10:de1c:
The next day, Aizawa went to school, even though he was afraid Kuwabata would take revenge.
Aizawa was on edge at every break between classes.
(What do I do if Kuwabata comes?)
That's what he kept thinking, but nothing happened, and the school day ended.{p}
rows.10:dfb8:
Aizawa was beaten like a punching bag.
Beaten and battered, Aizawa cried out,
"I'm sorry, but I just had to know.
If a person falls off a roof, do they die, or what happens?"
That was the reason he screamed, I'm told.
And then Kuwabata,{p}
rows.10:e0ac:
"Huh? You too.........?"
he said, and suddenly he stopped hitting him.{p}
rows.10:e104:
The two of them sat down and talked about what happens when someone jumps off a roof.
A strange friendship was born.
From that day on, they talked about it every single day.
The talk gradually escalated, until they were even talking about resuming the experiment.
Then they picked out a teacher they didn't like as their target, and drew up a plan.{p}
rows.10:e310:
"Nobody's fallen down there."
The teacher said this as he peered down.
Kuwabata, who had been hiding, made sure the teacher was there, then ran at him and slammed into him.
And the teacher went falling.
"............I can't really tell from here."{p}
rows.10:e3fc:
Aizawa said this, and the two of them hurried down the stairs to see whether the teacher was dead or alive.
It was after school and the place was deserted, so luckily no one came to gather around.{p}
rows.10:e4b0:
By the time the two of them got there, a pool of blood had already spread out wide around the teacher, who lay limp and motionless.
They watched closely for a while, but there was no sign of movement.
When they touched him, the body had already gone cold.
"...He's dead, all right."
Kuwabata smiled with satisfaction.{p}
rows.10:e5e0:
Now that they knew the result, the two of them were satisfied.
Relieved, they both slept soundly that night for the first time in a long while.{p}
rows.10:e650:
The next day at school, everyone was talking about the teacher.
The police were called in, and an investigation began.
And they found out that the teacher had met with Aizawa before dying.
The police questioned Aizawa, but he told them he didn't know anything.{p}
rows.10:e744:
That night, the two of them arranged to meet on the school roof to discuss what to do next.
Aizawa suggested the park, but Kuwabata insisted the roof was better.
When Aizawa reached the roof, Kuwabata was already there.
"What do we do now...?"
When Aizawa said this, Kuwabata answered,
"Easy.
You just kill yourself out of remorse for your crime."{p}
rows.10:e8b0:
Kuwabata grabbed Aizawa and drove him back toward the railing.
"You've gotta try it yourself, right?"{p}
rows.10:e910:
He was trying to throw Aizawa off the roof.
The two of them grappled, and Aizawa shoved Kuwabata away with all his might.{p}
rows.10:e994:
With that, Kuwabata fell into the schoolyard below.
Aizawa sank down onto the rooftop.
(Now it'll look like Kuwabata killed the teacher, then felt remorse and killed himself.)
It's all over now, he thought.
Then he leaned over to look down at Kuwabata from the roof.{p}
rows.10:eaa4:
Then he saw Kuwabata's and the teacher's faces floating in midair.
They looked happy, and they were saying this:
"How wonderful."
"Magnificent."
"Come on, Aizawa, you too."
"It's all thanks to you, Aizawa.
Who knew it'd be such a great place?"
"Kuwabata, by rights this isn't a place someone like you should be able to come."
"Aw, don't say that."
Aizawa had always been interested in jumping.
He couldn't hold himself back any longer.
"Kuwabata... Sir..."
He climbed over the railing and jumped.{p}
rows.10:ec7c:
As he fell, Aizawa thought only of getting to where they were, as fast as he could.
But it was just as he was about to reach the teacher and Kuwabata.{p}
rows.10:ed24:
Suddenly the teacher's and Kuwabata's faces twisted into hideous masks.
"Wahaha... haha..."
"Heh heh... heh..."
The two faces laughed eerily.
"You're coming to hell with us."
That's what Kuwabata said.
Aizawa regretted it, but it was already too late.
It had been a trap.{p}
rows.10:ee34:
The next day, the bodies of Aizawa and Kuwabata were found in the schoolyard.
There was no suicide note, and no connection between the two was ever found, so the case went cold...
But afterwards, something strange happened.
When summer vacation ended that year, the science teacher was looking over the students' independent research reports, and found one submitted jointly by Aizawa and Kuwabata, who should have died before the break.
It had this title:
"On Throwing Oneself from the Roof"
Its contents were roughly what I've just told you.{p}
rows.10:f020:
I happened to read that report once.
But a teacher stopped me partway through, so I never found out what the last part said.
I think it described the world they went to after they died.
{a}{f:,|,} if you ever happen to see that report, please tell me what was written there.{p}That's as far as the story I know goes.
Next person, please.{p}
rows.10:f2d8:
The next day, Aizawa went to school, thinking Kuwabata's body from the day before would have been found and there would be an uproar.
But there was nothing but the usual scene of students arriving at school.
Puzzled, Aizawa went to the spot from the day before.
(Maybe nobody's found him yet.)
That's what he was thinking.
But there was nothing there.
There wasn't even the bloodstain that had spread so vividly the day before.
Aizawa searched the area for quite a long time, but in the end he found nothing.
Uneasy as he was, he went on to his classroom.{p}
rows.10:f4e8:
The next day at school, he still heard nothing about Kuwabata.
And even after another week had passed, no one knew where Kuwabata was.
In the end, the police and the school wrote Kuwabata off as a runaway.
Kuwabata had always had problems in his life, so no one looked too deeply into the cause.
(Did the teachers cover it up because they were afraid of a scandal...?)
He even entertained such a convenient idea.
So, to make sure that Kuwabata was dead, Aizawa decided to continue the experiment.{p}
rows.10:f828:
But the next day, the body had vanished again.
(Something's wrong. Something's going on...)
And once again, the school wrote it off as a runaway.
After a while, he decided to lure out another delinquent and do the experiment once more.
This time, he planned to watch over the body all night.{p}
rows.10:f93c:
Aizawa made his prey inhale chloroform, and once again pushed it off the roof.
Then he ran down the stairs to check.
"Definitely dead."
Satisfied, he hid in the shadow of a nearby tree and waited for something to happen.{p}
rows.10:fa24:
But as the night wore on, he began to doze off.
And when he came to, the body was already gone.
Startled, he jumped to his feet.
"Huh? Where did it go?"{p}
rows.10:fae4:
There was no sign of anyone around, nor anything at all out of the ordinary.
It was just as Aizawa was about to start walking aimlessly.
Suddenly he sensed something behind him.
When he turned around, there stood the three delinquents he had pushed off so far.{p}
rows.10:fbec:
The three delinquents looked just as they had after falling from the roof, covered in wounds.
They slowly began walking toward Aizawa.
The ground was slick with the blood flowing from their bodies.
Aizawa slipped and caught himself with his hands on the ground, too terrified and stunned to move.
The delinquents grabbed him by both arms and dragged him up to the roof.
The three delinquents hoisted Aizawa up and threw him out over the railing.
That's right, Aizawa died.{p}
rows.10:fda4:
The next day, the school was in an uproar.
Not because Aizawa's body had been found.
But because, after the two who had gone missing, another two had gone missing.
In other words, Aizawa's body had gone off somewhere too.
The police began searching for the four of them, but nothing definite turned up.
There were reports that the four had been seen shuffling along a road on the day Aizawa went missing, but...
It was decided that they had run away from home.
In the end, the only ones who know the truth are me and all of you.{p}
rows.10:ffac:
Why do I know all this, you ask?
The truth is, I was receiving reports on the experiment's results all along.
The final experiment?
Oh, I was watching.
To confirm that the reports on the experiments weren't lies.
Why was I receiving reports?
I'll leave that to your imagination...{p}Well then, next person, please.{p}
rows.10:100bc:
Should he hit them with the bat...? Aizawa considered.
But he had already tried that.
So this time, he decided to try strangling his prey.
Aizawa wrapped his hands around the neck of the friend he had called out, and squeezed with all his strength.{p}
rows.10:101b4:
The friend's eyes went wide in disbelief.
No, perhaps they were bulging out in agony.
"It's not enough.
No matter what I do, it's never enough..."
Aizawa kept muttering it over and over, as if delirious.
And then... he killed his friend right there.
"No good.
Now I can't carry out the experiment..."
Aizawa staggered off in search of his next prey.{p}
rows.10:1032c:
Then he saw figures up ahead.
There were three of them.
They seemed to be wearing school uniforms.
Aizawa smiled.
My next experimental subjects have appeared.
...That's what he thought.
It seems he had already lost all sound judgment.
Someone had thrown a juice bottle into the park's trash can.
Aizawa picked it up and ran toward the figures.
But just then... someone's hands wrapped around his neck.
"Wha...!"
The hands were cold as a corpse's, stiff as if in rigor mortis, with the tendons standing out.
"Sto...!"
Aizawa tried to shake the hands off.
And the moment he desperately turned around... he saw it.{p}
rows.10:105a8:
The friend he had killed only moments ago, strangling him...
The face was drained of blood, and the eyes bulged just as they had at the moment of death.
The eyes were open wide, so wide, as if they were about to pop out.
Aizawa's neck was squeezed with tremendous force.
The juice bottle slipped from his limp hand and fell to the ground.
He could no longer even make a sound, only a burp-like gurgle from his throat.
The three up ahead came walking toward him.
At the same time, he heard laughter.
It sounded like they were laughing at Aizawa.
The three came right up in front of him.
Their faces... were those of the delinquents Aizawa had killed before.
All their faces were hideously twisted.
Those were exactly the expressions they had worn when they were killed.{p}
rows.10:1085c:
Aizawa was strangled to death by the dead.
It was all a result he had brought on himself.
But Aizawa was a pitiful person too.
He had craved his experiments so badly, and yet when it came time for him to die, he was strangled to death down on the dirt.
He must surely regret that.
Oh, yes, Aizawa's ghost appears at this school.
If you look down from the roof, Aizawa's face rises up from the ground.
They say the eyes in that face are wide open, just as when he was strangled...{p}That's the end of my story.
Well then, let's hear the next person's story.{p}
rows.10:10a78: He had already tried hitting them with a bat and making them inhale chloroform.{p}
rows.10:10acc:
So this time, Aizawa decided to try strangling his prey.
He tightened his grip carefully, so as not to kill.
And then the friend went limp.
Aizawa tried to stuff his guinea pig into the burlap sack he'd prepared in advance.
That was when he realized the friend was dead.{p}
rows.10:10c04:
"So people die this easily."
It sounded as though he had found the answer he'd longed for from the bottom of his heart.
And on his face was an expression almost like peace, as if he'd been released from tension for the first time in ages.
Aizawa left his friend's body where it lay and began walking through the streets at night.
He no longer cared at all about the experiment of dropping people from the roof.
He had found a bigger answer than what happens when a person falls from a roof.
Then, as a car was about to pass in front of Aizawa, he suddenly leapt out in front of it.
They say Aizawa was smiling at that moment.{p}
rows.10:10e20:
...They say his face in death was peaceful.
Huh? How do I know this story, you ask?
The truth is, a letter came to me afterwards.
It had no postmark and no address.
This story was written in that letter.
After all, I was the one who listened to him most earnestly.
Did he die having truly felt how fleeting human life is?
Or did he die satisfied, having learned the answer to his question?
That's written at the end of the letter, but I haven't read it.
I'm afraid that if I read it, I'd choose death too.
If you have the courage to look, I'll show it to you sometime.{p}That ends my story.
Next person, please.{p}
rows.10:11058:
But he couldn't bring himself to throw himself off just like that.
He still had to carry out the experiment......that's what he thought.
But someone pushed him from behind.
And so he fell from the roof...
Toward the ground.
Or perhaps, toward the depths of the earth...
And the place where his soul ends up may well be hell.{p}
rows.10:11318:
I see.
If you say you don't want to know, that's fine too.
It's a shame, but it can't be helped.
Personally, I would have loved to take you to where Aizawa is.{p}...Well then, let's hand things over to the next person.
Who's going to tell us the next story?{p}
rows.10:1141c:
I see.
You're not interested.
But should you really be saying that?
Aizawa is still here at this school, you know.{p}Don't you want to know where he is?
rows.10:114d8:
Very well, I'll tell you.
Aizawa is still on the roof.{p}
rows.10:11520:
...I see.
Sometimes you have to sidestep important matters for the sake of your own safety, don't you?
If that's how you feel, I won't say anything more.{p}...Let's hear the next person's story.
Now, whose turn is it next?{p}
rows.10:117c8:
...I thought you'd say that.
There's something here that puts people in that frame of mind.{p}
rows.10:1181c:
What's the matter?
Don't you want to meet Aizawa?
Go on, say it.
.........
You're not going to say it?
Then I'll say it.
You look down at the schoolyard like this and call out.
Aizawa! Let's begin the experi...{p}
rows.10:11904:
"Stop it!"
{f:I|I} clung to Arai.
Because he looked like he was about to jump...
"Arai, that's enough."
{f:I|I} said it desperately.
"I have a bad feeling about this.
Let's go back to the club room.
I don't care if we don't get to meet Aizawa.
Please, let's go back..."
Arai frowned.
But {f:I|I} forced everyone to come back to the club room.
We had to avoid any more danger.{p}
rows.10:11ad0:
When we got back to the club room, everyone fell silent, eyes cast down.
Arai, too, kept his mouth shut, glaring at the floor.
A strange atmosphere hung in the room.
{f:But|Still,} we couldn't just stop here.
{f:I|I} called out to everyone.{p}"Well then... let's move on to the next story..."{p}
rows.10:11bec:
"Let's stop..."
{f:I|I} was utterly exhausted.
We couldn't go on any longer.
If this kept up, even my own life might be in danger.
I couldn't shake that feeling.
{f:We|We} broke up and went home just like that.{p}
rows.10:11e10:
Then, while sorting through my things in the newspaper club room... I found a notebook.
On its cover was written the name Nobuhiko Aizawa.
This name...
{f:I|I} opened the notebook.
But there was nothing but blank page after blank page{f:.|.}
"There's nothing written in i...
rows.10:11f3c:
On the notebook's last page, {f:my|my} name was written.
What could this notebook mean?
As I stared at it, {f:my|my} name slowly faded away.
And in its place, new words began to surface...{p}
rows.10:12028:
{f:I|I} fled from the club room.
The words that had appeared in the notebook were these:
"Let's begin the experiment..."
The ghost story from that day came back to me.
{f:I|I} was the only one who had felt things were peaceful once we stopped the seven wonders stories.
Even though {f:I|I} had stopped the stories, the supernatural phenomena themselves really did exist at this school{f:.|.}
And the next victim would be...{p}
rows.10:12184:
A sharp pain shot through the back of {f:my|my} head.
Who{f:'s that|'s that}?
What on earth for...
"For the experiment."
I heard someone's voice.
"Now, Aizawa, let's begin the experiment..."
It was a voice I recognized.{p}
rows.10:1224c:
As {f:my|my} consciousness faded, the face of the person I had met at the seven wonders storytelling that day came into view.
His name was, if I remember right... Arai... Ara...
"Now, the time has come for you to set out on your journey too.
Let's go together.
Look... Aizawa is here too..."
Over Arai's shoulder floated a huge skull.
I shouldn't have stopped the seven wonders meeting partway through.
I shouldn't have poked my nose into this school's supernatural phenomena so half-heartedly{f:...|...}
{f:I|I} would probably become material for Aizawa's experiment{f:.|.}
Arai was grinning.
There was no escape.
No escape from this reality.
Would the last thing {f:I|I} saw be the sky{f:,|,} or blood splattered across the ground{f:?|?}
That, I would soon find out{f:.|.}{p}
